texts.title: Happy enough?
texts.hook.h1.frame: Recall your best day… measuring it?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: recall the best day of your life… were you measuring your joy?
texts.hook.h2.frame: Chase happiness… and it flies away?
texts.hook.h2: They say happiness is like a butterfly: the more you chase it, the more it flies off… really?
texts.hook.h3.frame: Waiting all year… then: that's it?
texts.hook.h3: I wait a whole year for the holiday… and on its first day I say: is that it?
texts.hook.h4: 8,331 people: those who care more about happiness… less happy, or happier?
texts.hook.h5: And you? On a day out, do you ask yourself: am I happy enough?
texts.s1.n1: This is Nour, on the work trip to the sea.
texts.s1.l1: I have to enjoy every minute!
texts.s1.l2: Am I happy enough?… It should be more!
texts.s1.l4: Lovely… but not what I imagined.
texts.s1.a2: And on the best day of your life… was there a meter?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time, no meter.
texts.s1.l6: Yes! Come, let's sit with the others.
texts.book.card: Wanting more good feelings… is itself a bad feeling.
texts.book.l1: The book says: the harder you chase feeling good… the less content you are.
texts.book.l2: Because every « am I happy? »… reminds you of what you lack.
texts.verdict.card: 8,331 Dutch · valuing happiness: generally better · valuing more: same satisfaction, mixed feelings
texts.verdict.nuance: Not the wish… worrying about your joy is linked to feeling worse, and seeking it with people to more satisfaction.
texts.verdict.l2: Sometimes they found happiness-chasers less happy… sometimes better off.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it: instead of measuring your joy… share it with someone. It may help.
texts.takeaway.orientation: If joy has been missing for weeks, talk to a psychologist.
texts.share: Send this to someone who measures their joy on every day out.
